title: Parse, TryParse and Convert
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and behavior of parse, tryparse and convert in C#.
Choose an appropriate type for a simple application scenario.
Read and explain original C# code that demonstrates the lesson concepts.
Predict deterministic program output and identify common mistakes.
Compile and execute a small .NET 10 console example to verify the result.

understand.concept: Text from users or files often needs to become a typed value. Parse converts valid text or throws a format-related exception, TryParse reports success without using an exception for ordinary invalid input, and Convert provides conversion methods with defined null and rounding behavior.
understand.whyItMatters: Reliable input conversion prevents crashes and lets applications explain invalid data clearly.
understand.analogy: Parse is like asking a strict reader to interpret a value; TryParse is like asking whether the reader can interpret it and receiving a yes/no result.
understand.analogyLimit: These methods do not validate the business meaning of a value. A successfully parsed age can still be outside an application's acceptable range.

explain.narrative:
## Parse

Methods such as int.Parse convert valid numeric text to a typed value. They throw exceptions when the input is null, malformed or outside the target type's range. Use Parse when invalid input is exceptional and should be handled accordingly.

## TryParse

TryParse returns a bool indicating whether conversion succeeded and writes the parsed result through an out parameter. It is usually the better choice for ordinary user input because invalid text is an expected possibility.

## Convert

System.Convert offers conversion methods such as ToInt32. Its behavior is not identical to a cast: for example, Convert.ToInt32(double) rounds to the nearest integer using midpoint-to-even behavior. Convert.ToInt32(null) returns zero.

## Culture and validation

Numeric text can use culture-specific decimal separators. When data is exchanged in a machine-readable format, choose an explicit culture such as CultureInfo.InvariantCulture. Parsing validates format and range, not application-specific rules.

## Baseline

Examples target .NET 10 and C# 14.

examples.title: Parse valid integer text
examples.explanation: int.Parse converts the valid text to an int, which can then participate in arithmetic.

examples.title: Use TryParse for invalid input
examples.explanation: TryParse reports failure without throwing for ordinary malformed input. The out value is zero when parsing fails for int.

examples.title: Convert a numeric value
examples.explanation: Convert.ToInt32(double) rounds to the nearest integer rather than truncating like an explicit cast.

examples.title: Parse with invariant culture
examples.explanation: InvariantCulture makes the decimal separator explicit and avoids dependence on the machine's current culture.

examples.title: Handle Parse failure
examples.explanation: Malformed text causes FormatException. The example handles that specific failure and displays a useful message.

practise.guidedTask: Create a .NET 10 console project and reproduce a small scenario that demonstrates parse, tryparse and convert. Build it, run it, compare the exact output and explain why each value has its resulting type or state.
practise.independentTask: Design an original C# console example using parse, tryparse and convert in a learner-registration, inventory or order-processing scenario. Include at least two meaningful cases, document expected output and explain one limitation or edge case.

questions.prompt: Which method returns a Boolean success result when parsing text?
questions.explanation: TryParse reports whether conversion succeeded and supplies the value through an out parameter.

questions.prompt: What happens when int.Parse receives malformed text?
questions.explanation: Parse throws FormatException when the text is not in a valid integer format.
Convert.ToInt32(double) rounds to the nearest integer; 12.6 rounds to 13.

questions.prompt: Why use CultureInfo.InvariantCulture for machine-readable numeric text?
questions.answer: To make formatting rules independent of the current user culture
options: To make formatting rules independent of the current user culture
To accept every possible number format
To convert all numbers to strings
questions.explanation: InvariantCulture provides stable culture-independent parsing and formatting rules.

questions.prompt: Does successful parsing guarantee a value is valid for the application?
questions.answer: No, business rules must still be checked
options: No, business rules must still be checked
Yes, parsing checks all business rules
No, parsed values cannot be used
questions.explanation: Parsing checks whether text can be represented by the target type, not whether it meets domain-specific rules.
